reason: The cited evidence (E1–E4) directly supports premises 1–4 with specific microstructural and electrochemical data from cold-rolled and heat-treated Cantor alloy. However, premise 5—that passive layer integrity governs the coupled tribo-corrosion response—is not addressed in the cited passages, which only examine static corrosion, leaving a key mechanistic link unsupported.
premises: Cold rolling induces grain refinement and high residual stress in Cantor alloy
Residual stress and fine grains weaken the passive layer, reducing corrosion resistance
Heat treatment at 1100 °C relieves residual stress and coarsens grains via recrystallization
Adequate recrystallization yields a more uniform, robust passive layer that improves corrosion resistance
Passive layer integrity governs both wear and corrosion rates under coupled tribo-corrosion
